question: What performance gains did the wireless sensor network and MRI computing studies report for their respective optimizations?
expected_answer: The sensor-network paper reports up to about 3.5% lower energy consumption, a 44% longer network life cycle and 185% more packets sent than LEACH. The MRI team reports shorter processing time with its GPU implementation.

W2991563224: Energy consumption fell by up to about 3.5%.
Sensor network life cycle increased by 44%.
Packet count increased by 185% relative to LEACH.
W4230116451: Identifies the GPU MRI denoising case.
Execution time is the reported computational outcome.

evidence.title: Energy efficiency of organized cluster election method in wireless sensor networks
evidence.quote: The energy consumption of WSN has been reduced up to about 3.5 %.
evidence.supports: Energy consumption fell by up to about 3.5%.

evidence.title: Energy efficiency of organized cluster election method in wireless sensor networks
evidence.quote: The network life cycle is prolonged by 44 %.
evidence.supports: Sensor network life cycle increased by 44%.

evidence.title: Energy efficiency of organized cluster election method in wireless sensor networks
evidence.quote: The number of packets sent has been increased by 185 % than LEACH.
evidence.supports: Packet count increased by 185% relative to LEACH.

evidence.title: A GPU parallel optimised blockwise NLM algorithm in a distributed computing system
evidence.quote: In the case study of the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), for improving the quality of denoising and helping the real-time diagnosis, we have implemented a GPU parallel algorithm based on the optimised blockwise non-local means (OB-NLM) method.
evidence.supports: Identifies the GPU MRI denoising case.

evidence.title: A GPU parallel optimised blockwise NLM algorithm in a distributed computing system
evidence.quote: Experimental results have shown a significant improvement of healthcare processing practice in terms of execution time.
evidence.supports: Execution time is the reported computational outcome.

rationale: One study reports network-level outcomes, while the other assesses the time needed for image processing.
limitations: Execution time has no numerical speedup in the MRI abstract. The percentages belong to the sensor network.

question: How do shape-coded composites and papal annual medals each carry information in a physical object?
expected_answer: Controlled shapes of embedded nanoparticles encode information in composites. The medals use images on their reverses and commemorate a papal achievement from the preceding year.

W3027457624: The composite stores information in controlled nanoparticle morphologies.
W2394633461: The survey identifies reverse-side images as its material.

evidence.title: “Shape-Coding”: Morphology-Based Information System for Polymers and Composites
evidence.quote: We describe a universal method to store information in fiber-reinforced composites based on solid-state in situ reduction leading to embedded nanoparticles with controlled morphologies.
evidence.supports: The composite stores information in controlled nanoparticle morphologies.

evidence.title: Pressing Metal, Pressing Politics: Papal Annual Medals, 1605–1700
evidence.quote: This article surveys images depicted on the reverses of papal annual medals in the seventeenth century, beginning in 1605 under Paul V (r. 1605–21) with the first confirmed annual medal, and ending in 1700 at the conclusion of the papacy of Innocent XII (r. 1691–1700), a reign that marked a distinct change in papal politics in advance of the eighteenth century.
evidence.supports: The survey identifies reverse-side images as its material.

evidence.title: Pressing Metal, Pressing Politics: Papal Annual Medals, 1605–1700
evidence.quote: Annual medals are a unique iteration of papal commemorative medals and they celebrate an important papal achievement from the preceding year.
evidence.supports: The annual issues commemorate achievements.

rationale: Each source supplies a different physical carrier and a different meaning attached to it.
limitations: This comparison of encoding and commemoration implies no historical influence between the practices.

question: How did researchers capture an image of the NSTX divertor, and what instrument did astronomers use to map the Moon at L band?
expected_answer: At NSTX, a sapphire window and movable in-vessel mirror image the divertor, and a coherent fiber optic bundle carries the image through a filter to a fast camera. The lunar team used the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory Synthesis Telescope.

W2084709926: Identifies the window, mirror and region imaged.
Traces the image to the filtered camera.
W2096307598: Identifies the observing band, target and telescope.

evidence.title: NSTX tangential divertor camera
evidence.quote: A reentrant sapphire window with a moveable in-vessel mirror images the divertor region from the center stack out to R∼80 cm and views the x-point for most plasma configurations.
evidence.supports: Identifies the window, mirror and region imaged.

evidence.title: NSTX tangential divertor camera
evidence.quote: A coherent fiber optic bundle transmits the image through a remotely selected filter to a fast camera, for example, a 40 500 frames/s photron complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor camera.
evidence.supports: Traces the image to the filtered camera.

evidence.title: New radio observations of the Moon atLband
evidence.quote: We present results of new radio observations of the Moon at L band with the synthesis telescope of the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory Synthesis Telescope.
evidence.supports: Identifies the observing band, target and telescope.

rationale: Each abstract identifies how its observing system forms or receives an image of a spatially extended target.
limitations: The instruments observe different sources. Their spatial resolutions cannot be compared from these passages alone.

question: How did the economic convergence and air–rail fare papers solve different modeling problems?
expected_answer: The convergence paper proposed time-varying parameters estimated by Kalman filtering to test convergence. The fare paper optimized prices in a bi-level model, using particle swarm for the upper level and successive averages for the lower level.

W2078771716: Defines the convergence testing framework and estimation method.
W4309030044: Names the fare model and assigns each solver to a level.

evidence.title: Measuring Economic Convergence
evidence.quote: These two considerations lead us to a preferred definition of convergence and a proposed framework for testing, based on a time varying parameter formulation and estimation by Kalman filter techniques.
evidence.supports: Defines the convergence testing framework and estimation method.

evidence.title: Market competition oriented air-rail ticket fare optimization
evidence.quote: The stochastic user equilibrium model based on elastic demand is used to establish a bi-level programming model for the optimization of fares; the upper and lower models are solved using the particle swarm algorithm and method of successive averages, respectively.
evidence.supports: Names the fare model and assigns each solver to a level.

rationale: The first source supplies an estimation framework and the second supplies the ordered pair of optimization methods.
limitations: The methods address different objectives. These descriptions supply no comparison of their accuracy.

question: What difficulty with historical testimony does the essay comparing the 1930s and 1960s describe, and how does the Italian oral-history essay characterize the making of an interview?
expected_answer: The first writer says contemporaries and younger collaborators often lacked sufficient distance from their own time to compare the decades. The Italian essay describes interviews as stories from below co-authored by the interviewee and an empathic interviewer.

W2326480042: Names the decades the author wants to compare.
Identifies the writer's concern about historical distance.
W4381572413: Describes the relationship that produces interview testimony.

evidence.title: Between the 30s and the 60s
evidence.quote: I strongly doubt if we will ever understandand fully evaluate -the 60s without placing it against the background of another radical decade, the 30s.
evidence.supports: Names the decades the author wants to compare.

evidence.title: Between the 30s and the 60s
evidence.quote: Having lived out both periods up to the hilt, I find that my older contemporaries as well as the younger people with whom I worked twenty years ago have seldom been able to distance themselves sufficiently from their time to draw these crucial comparisons adequately.
evidence.supports: Identifies the writer's concern about historical distance.

evidence.title: “First of all, let’s go learn something”
evidence.quote: Oral interviews are stories “from below”, where the authorship is shared between the interviewed people and an empathic interviewer.
evidence.supports: Describes the relationship that produces interview testimony.

rationale: The retrospective essay supplies a problem of perspective. The oral-history account supplies a distinct description of authorship.
limitations: The Italian essay does not establish that shared authorship resolves the other writer's difficulty.

question: Whose judgments does the PNM teaching-evaluation system collect, and what reader-dependent measurement did the mammography team try to automate?
expected_answer: At PNM, students evaluate lecturers' teaching and learning processes. In the mammography study, the authors used image processing and penalized regression to mimic the semiautomated Cumulus measure of mammographic density.

W4234628002: Identifies the students and the object of their evaluations.
W1979727947: Names reader dependence as a measurement problem.
Identifies the automated method and its reference measure.

evidence.title: Sistem Informasi Terintegrasi Evaluasi Kegiatan Mengajar Dosen Sebagai Implementasi Sistem Penjaminan Mutu Internal
evidence.quote: To realize the objectives of SPMI Dikti, it is needed an information technology based system that can manage the result of quality control from PNM which can be accessed via online by students privately and allows the students to evaluate the teaching and learning process of the lecturers.
evidence.supports: Identifies the students and the object of their evaluations.

evidence.title: High-throughput mammographic-density measurement: a tool for risk prediction of breast cancer
evidence.quote: INTRODUCTION: Mammographic density (MD) is a strong, independent risk factor for breast cancer, but measuring MD is time consuming and reader dependent.
evidence.supports: Names reader dependence as a measurement problem.

evidence.title: High-throughput mammographic-density measurement: a tool for risk prediction of breast cancer
evidence.quote: We use a public domain image-processing software for the fully automated analysis of MD and penalized regression to construct a measure that mimics a well-established semiautomated measure (Cumulus).
evidence.supports: Identifies the automated method and its reference measure.

rationale: Both studies deal with assessments that involve people. One builds a system to gather their judgments, while the other seeks to reproduce an established measure automatically.
limitations: Collecting evaluations online does not imply automated scoring of teaching quality. Mimicking Cumulus does not validate an individual cancer diagnosis.

question: How did the dialysis knee-replacement study and the esophageal radiotherapy pilot monitor what happened after treatment?
expected_answer: The knee study used clinical and radiographic evaluations, American Knee Society Scores, and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index. The radiotherapy study checked cardiac device function before therapy and after every irradiation.

W2761455282: Specifies the knee evaluations and scoring instruments.
W4391351014: Specifies the timing and target of the device checks.

evidence.title: Perioperative Complications of Total Knee Arthroplasty in Dialysis Patients
evidence.quote: All patients had complete clinical and radiographic evaluations, and the outcome was scored using American Knee Society Scores and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index.
evidence.supports: Specifies the knee evaluations and scoring instruments.

evidence.title: Effects of Ionizing Radiation on Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices (CIEDs) in Patients with Esophageal Cancer Undergoing Radiotherapy: A Pilot Study
evidence.quote: All patients underwent systemic evaluation including pre-therapeutic cardiological examinations of the CIED functionality and after every single irradiation.
evidence.supports: Specifies the timing and target of the device checks.

rationale: Only the orthopedic source supplies its joint assessments, and only the pilot specifies fraction-by-fraction device checks.
limitations: Different cohorts and endpoints preclude a joint complication rate.

question: How did the astrocyte researchers distinguish the channels involved in permeability, and how did the mouse copy-number study assess whether genomic differences mattered for expression?
expected_answer: The astrocyte study combined pharmacological tests with Px1 knockdown and astrocytes from Cx43 knockout mice. The mouse study compared changes in copy number with changes in gene expression and found that a simple correlation did not hold in every case.

W2039836112: Specifies the tests used to differentiate channel types.
Relates a channel type to cell permeability.
W2076293586: Identifies the comparison used to assess functional relevance.

evidence.title: FGF-1 induces ATP release from spinal astrocytes in culture and opens pannexin and connexin hemichannels
evidence.quote: HC types were differentiated pharmacologically and by Px1 knockdown with siRNA and by use of astrocytes from Cx43 knockout mice.
evidence.supports: Specifies the tests used to differentiate channel types.

evidence.title: FGF-1 induces ATP release from spinal astrocytes in culture and opens pannexin and connexin hemichannels
evidence.quote: Increased permeability of cells exposed to FGF-1 or ATP for 2 h was mediated largely by Px1 HCs activated by P2X(7) receptors.
evidence.supports: Relates a channel type to cell permeability.

evidence.title: Copy number variants in two mouse models of affective disorders
evidence.quote: To test the functional relevance of these CNVs, we associated changes in copy numbers with changes in gene expression.
evidence.supports: Identifies the comparison used to assess functional relevance.

evidence.title: Copy number variants in two mouse models of affective disorders
evidence.quote: A simple correlation between gene dosage and gene expression could not be found in all cases.
evidence.supports: Qualifies the observed dosage–expression relationship.

rationale: The studies give two ways of examining functional relevance. One distinguishes channel types by perturbation, and the other checks whether measured changes covary.
limitations: A dosage–expression association cannot establish the role of a channel in cultured cells. The findings belong to different experimental systems.

question: How do the Chinese grain-production article and the comment on plant closings describe income outcomes under the conditions each discusses?
expected_answer: The grain article reports no loss of farmers' total income as grain output rose. The comment attributes to Nord and Ting the claim that workers given over two months' voluntary warning faced smaller earnings losses.

W2906067930: Gives the scope and direction of farm income.
W2130236240: Attributes the voluntary-notice finding and distinguishes it from later legislation.

evidence.title: Research on the Phenomenon That the Increase of Grain Production Did Not Cause the Harvest Paradox in China from 2003 to 2014
evidence.quote: The phenomenon was found it didn’t cause the loss of farmers' total income that the grain production in China had increased for 11 years from 2003 to 2014, which was inconsistent with the Harvest Paradox in economics.
evidence.supports: Gives the scope and direction of farm income.

evidence.title: The Impact of Advance Notice: A Comment on a Study by Nord and Ting
evidence.quote: In their analysis of the effects of advance notification of plant closings, Nord and Ting (ILR Review, July 1991) claim that much can be expected of current legislation that mandates a 60-day prenotification standard because the outcomes of voluntary arrangements, in an interval preceding implementation of the legislation, point to substantial reductions in both joblessness and earnings losses for workers given over two months' warning of their impending layoff.
evidence.supports: Attributes the voluntary-notice finding and distinguishes it from later legislation.

rationale: The grain paper provides a sector-level income observation. The comment reports another study's worker-level claim.
limitations: The voluntary-notice observation cannot by itself establish the impact of the later statutory standard. The texts concern different populations.

question: What role does listening play in the synodality essay, and who shares authorship of a spoken account in the Italian oral-history essay?
expected_answer: The synodality essay treats listening as an outward practice alongside collaboration and leadership, drawing an analogy to inner work in IFS. The oral-history essay gives the empathic interviewer and the interviewee shared authorship.

W7215137876: Places listening among synodal practices and draws the inner/outer analogy.

evidence.title: Emotional Maturity in the Light of Synodality: Contributions from Internal Family System Therapy
evidence.quote: It examines similarities between the IFS way of dealing with the inner world of the person and Synodal practices like listening, collaboration, and leadership in the outer world.
evidence.supports: Places listening among synodal practices and draws the inner/outer analogy.

evidence.title: “First of all, let’s go learn something”
evidence.quote: Oral interviews are stories “from below”, where the authorship is shared between the interviewed people and an empathic interviewer.
evidence.supports: Defines the participants' shared authorship.

rationale: Both accounts attend to interpersonal practice. Only the synodality essay makes the IFS analogy, and only the oral-history essay assigns authorship.
limitations: Shared attention to listening does not imply that the oral historian uses IFS.
